title: Halting during a print simulation
statement: Let a counter program $P$ have a print instruction at state $l$, printing register $r$ and continuing at state $l'$. Let its simulated register values be $\rho$, and let $ps,o_0\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every value $\rho(s)$ is at most $B$, $ps\le B$, and $p<o_0+\rho(r)\le B$. Suppose the two oracle answers on inputs pairing $n$ ones with the binary expansion of $h$ are, respectively, whether $h$ is less than the length of a fixed word $u$, and the bit of $u$ at position $h$ (with false used beyond its end). For every $d,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $o_0+j+d=p$, the compiled simulation on the input pairing $n$ ones with the binary expansion of $p$, started at the print-processing state with original registers $\rho$, pointer value $ps$, output-position value $o_0+j$, and temporary value $j$, halts with answer true while satisfying the prescribed state and register bounds at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ has a print instruction at $l$ on register $r$, continuing at $l'$
Every original register value under $\rho$ is at most $B$
Oracle 0 answers whether $h<|u|$ on the specified paired input
Oracle 1 returns the bit of $u$ at position $h$, defaulting to false
